claim:
Text: "Video shows attack of French embassy in Sudan"
Claim author: Anmol Alphonso
Claim date: October 28, 2020
Claim origin: https://www.boomlive.in/fake-news/2012-embassy-attacks-in-sudan-falsely-shared-as-attack-on-french-embassy-10392
before_justification: The fact-check concludes that the claim is **refuted** because the video, [verified by BOOM](https://www.boomlive.in/fake-news/2012-embassy-attacks-in-sudan-falsely-shared-as-attack-on-french-embassy-10392), is actually from **September 2012** and shows protesters storming and setting fire to the **German Embassy in Khartoum**, Sudan, not the French embassy. The footage was authentic but was being falsely shared with a misleading context in 2020, with no official confirmation of any attack on the French embassy at that time.
after_justification: While the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed an attack on its embassy in Khartoum, Sudan, on October 28, 2020, the fact-check investigation by [BoomLive](https://www.boomlive.in/fake-news/2012-embassy-attacks-in-sudan-falsely-shared-as-attack-on-french-embassy-10392) reveals that the specific video in question is old footage from a 2012 event that has been falsely recirculated and misattributed to the 2020 attack, leading to the verdict that the claim is **refuted**.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Is there a verified video that clearly and undeniably shows a physical attack (such as an assault, explosion, or armed raid) occurring on the premises of the French embassy in Sudan?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: While the search result confirms that a coordinated attack on the French embassy in Khartoum, Sudan, occurred on October 28, 2020, and was verified by multiple reports, it does not provide any information about the existence or verification of a video showing the attack.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: "French embassy Khartoum" attack video 2020 On October 28, 2020, a coordinated attack on the French embassy in Khartoum, Sudan, was confirmed by multiple verified reports.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: According to official records from the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Sudanese government, was the French embassy in Khartoum, Sudan, the subject of a documented attack?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, according to official records, the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed and condemned an attack on their embassy in Sudan on October 28, 2020.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: "French embassy Khartoum" attack video 2020 On October 28, 2020, the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed and condemned an attack on their embassy in Sudan, supporting the video claim.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: What is the original date of the footage that is being presented as an attack on the French embassy in Sudan?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: The original date of the footage is October 28, 2020, as verified by Reuters and AFP.
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: "French embassy Khartoum" exterior photo Reuters and AFP verified the video shows the October 28, 2020 attack on the French embassy in Sudan.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Does the video footage used in the claim actually depict the French embassy in Khartoum, Sudan, or does it show a different building, embassy, or location?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, the video footage does depict the French embassy in Khartoum, Sudan. According to the search result, the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs officially confirmed and condemned the attack on their embassy, stating: "French ministry of foreign affairs confirmed and condemned an attack on their embassy in Sudan."
adopted_qa_evidence.scraped_text: "French embassy Khartoum" attack video 2020 On October 28, 2020, the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed and condemned an attack on their embassy in Sudan, supporting the video claim.

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Have credible, non-partisan news organizations (e.g., AFP, Reuters, BBC) reported on a genuine attack against the French embassy in Sudan around the date of October 28, 2020?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, according to the search result, credible news agencies Reuters and AFP verified the video and reported on the attack, with the source stating: "Reuters and AFP verified the video, confirming it shows the October 28, 2020 attack on the French embassy."

adopted_qa_evidence.question: Has the video referenced in the claim been previously used in other contexts or misattributed to a different event before this claim was made?
adopted_qa_evidence.answer: Yes, the video had been previously misattributed to a different event. The original fact-check article, which is the claim's source, states that it shows "2012 embassy attacks in Sudan falsely shared as attack on French embassy" in 2020.

CAIRO (AP) — Witnesses say Sudanese police have opened fire on protesters trying to climb the walls of the U.S. Embassy in Khartoum.
The witnesses say several thousands of Sudanese were protesting outside the embassy, trying to storm it in anger over an obscure file produced in the United States that denigrated the Prophet Muhammad.
It was not immediately clear if any protesters got into the embassy.
The witnesses said at least three protesters were hurt, seen motionless on the ground. There was no immediate confirmation whether they were dead.
The attack came as protests against the film spread around the Middle East and other Muslim countries, from Tunisia to Pakistan.

One protester was killed in the northern Lebanese city of Tripoli in clashes with security forces, after a crowd of protesters set fire to a KFC and an Arby’s restaurant.
Protesters hurled stones and glass at police in a furious melee that left 25 people wounded, 18 of them police.
Protests were held in cities from Egypt to Pakistan after weekly Friday Muslim prayers, where many clerics in their mosques sermons denounced an obscure movie produced in the United States that denigrated the Prophet Muhammad.
The spread of protests comes after attacks earlier this week on the U.S. Embassies in Cairo and the Yemeni capital Sanaa and on a U.S. consulate in Libya, where the ambassador and three other Americans were killed.

September 14, 2012 (KHARTOUM) – Hundreds of Sudanese protesters angered by an anti-Islam film made in the US attacked the premises of two Western diplomatic missions in the capital Khartoum on Friday, setting one of them on fire, eye witnesses told Sudan Tribune.
The protest was called for by hard-line Islamist groups and individuals to demonstrate against “Innocence of Muslims” an amateur internet film mocking the Prophet Mohammed.
The film already sparked popular outrage and concomitant protests outside US diplomatic missions across the Middle East.
According to witnesses, hundreds of protesters led mainly by Islamists started demonstrating on Friday in front of the German and British embassies on Al-Baladiya streets in downtown Khartoum.
The protesters later set the German embassy on fire. The protest is ongoing.

Despite poverty and rising prices activists haven’t sparked a movement comparable to what happened in Egypt or Tunisia.
Khartoum, Sudan – As the Arab Spring swept leaders from power in neighbouring countries, some Sudanese hoped that anti-government protests earlier this year would be the beginning of the end for long-ruling President Omar al-Bashir.
But a combination of heavy-handed tactics by Sudanese security forces, including beatings and arrests, coupled with other factors, meant the demonstrations vanished just as quickly as they arose.
When the anti-Islam video protests erupted in Khartoum, Sudan’s capital, some activists hoped the energy could somehow morph into anti-government protests.
They didn’t. In fact, they couldn’t. The Friday protests at the embassies were not just sanctioned but orchestrated by the government.
On Thursday night, government representatives met with sheikhs of the main mosques in the capital. They were told to encourage people in the sermon to go out and protest at the embassies.
Government representatives emphasised they wanted peaceful protests but were well-aware that some of the more conservative sheikhs were angry and planning to call on people to storm diplomatic missions in the name of the Prophet.
On September 13, government minivans took groups of protesters to the US Embassy, 20km south of Khartoum.
Three people were killed after police vehicles ran over demonstrators and government officials said they were not happy about violence undermining what they hoped would be choreographed protests.
Like other leaders in the Muslim world, Bashir had a difficult balancing act – he could not appear unsupportive of protests against a hugely offensive video, nor could he risk violent protests that make the country look ungovernable.
The protests also gave Bashir an opportunity to prove his religious credentials, after opponents accused him of abandoning them in recent years.
